theme: 3 terms on stopping the app on purpose: a crash that always happens, a check that runs only in debug builds, and a check that stays in release builds

terms.definition: A call to `fatalError` that always stops the app, in every build, for code that should never be reached.
terms.example: That `default` case can't happen, so a Fatal Error with a clear message is fine.

terms.definition: A check written with `assert` that stops the app when its condition is false, but only in debug builds.
terms.example: Add an Assertion here, so we notice the bad value while testing.

terms.definition: A check written with `precondition` that stops the app when its condition is false, even in release builds.
terms.example: A wrong index would corrupt the data, so use a Precondition, not an assert.

quizzes.question: In this code, which check would you add on the comment line, so it runs only in debug builds?
Which check keeps working in release builds and stops the app when its condition is false?
Which call always stops the app, in every build, without checking any condition?

video.title: Fatal Error, Assertion & Precondition | Day 70
video.description:
Learn to explain safety checks in Swift: Fatal Error, Assertion & Precondition, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Fatal Error - A call to `fatalError` that always stops the app, in every build, for code that should never be reached.
Assertion - A check written with `assert` that stops the app when its condition is false, but only in debug builds.
Precondition - A check written with `precondition` that stops the app when its condition is false, even in release builds.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Fatal Error, Assertion & Precondition in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
치명적 오류, 단언문, 전제 조건 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Fatal Error - A call to `fatalError` that always stops the app, in every build, for code that should never be reached.
한국어: 치명적 오류: 어떤 빌드에서든 항상 앱을 멈추는 `fatalError` 호출로, 절대 도달하면 안 되는 코드에 씀

Assertion - A check written with `assert` that stops the app when its condition is false, but only in debug builds.
한국어: 단언문: 조건이 거짓이면 앱을 멈추지만 디버그 빌드에서만 동작하는 `assert` 검사

Precondition - A check written with `precondition` that stops the app when its condition is false, even in release builds.
한국어: 전제 조건: 조건이 거짓이면 릴리스 빌드에서도 앱을 멈추는 `precondition` 검사

landscape.hook: Two checks, one function. Can you explain the difference in English?

dialogue.title: Why two checks?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `play` has two checks. Why not just one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They behave differently. The first one is an Assertion. It only runs in debug builds.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So in the App Store build, it's gone?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. An Assertion catches our own mistakes while we test.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the Precondition stays in release?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. A Precondition still crashes for users if the `rate` is too high.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Playing with broken data is worse. A Precondition stops it early.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A Fatal Error always crashes, in every build, with no condition to check.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Assertion for testing, Precondition for release, and Fatal Error when it can never happen.
A Fatal Error crashes in every build, no questions asked.
